_doc: The disc launcher: what the toy must do, and the design choices every part shares (kind default), so the disc, the bow, the sear, the magazine and the frame all read the same numbers. The sizing from these is worked in examples/bench/projects/launcher/README.md.
name: launcher

disc.rule: The disc's diameter: small enough to stack six in a hand-sized magazine, big enough to fly flat

disc_t.rule: The disc's thickness: ten layers, stiff enough not to flutter

disc_mass.rule: A disc's mass in PLA, solid: π × 15² × 2 mm³ × 1.26 g/cm³
disc_mass.source: Worked from disc, disc_t and pla.density; weigh a printed one

disc_energy.rule: The most kinetic energy a disc may leave with: the toy standards' threshold, above which a projectile needs a resilient tip. A hard PLA disc has none, so it stays under
disc_energy.source: ASTM F963-17 §4.20 and EN 71-1 §4.17 (projectile toys): over 0.08 J the striking face must be resilient and its kinetic energy per contact area under 2500 J/m². Check the current editions

energy.rule: The energy the bow stores at full draw: with the launch efficiency below, the disc leaves at about disc_energy

efficiency.rule: The share of the stored energy the disc leaves with: the rest moves the sled and the leaf itself. A guess until a disc is timed
efficiency.source: The sled and the leaf's moving share weigh about three times the disc (examples/bench/projects/launcher/README.md)

travel.rule: The bow's draw: how far the leaf bends from rest to cocked, and the stroke the sled is pushed through. Shorter draws need shorter leaves and store nearly as much, at a higher pull

overrun.rule: The sled's run past the leaves' rest, to its stop: the leaves let go before the sled stops

draw.rule: The pull at full draw: 2 × energy / travel for a leaf that is a linear spring. What the cocking ring and the sear carry

trigger_pull.rule: The trigger's pull at release, at most: light for a child, firm enough not to go off when knocked

trigger_travel.rule: The finger's travel from rest to release

feed.rule: The least the feeder presses the last disc down with: ten times its weight, so it drops whichever way the launcher points

spin_offset.rule: How far off the disc's centre line the sled's nose pushes, towards the bed wall: the push turns the disc, which rolls along the lid and leaves spinning, so it flies flat
spin_offset.source: The disc launcher's design (examples/bench/projects/launcher/README.md); the Nerf Vortex launches its discs the same way

flexure_width.rule: Every flexure's height off the bed (its width): 140 layers, under the disc's diameter, so they all fit between the bed wall and the lid

strain_limit.rule: The strain PLA may see in a flexure: 2%, the working guess until the flexure bench's plates are measured (examples/bench/projects/flexures/results.json). Near PLA's yield: don't leave the launcher cocked

grip.rule: The hand's hold on the grip, and the hardest knock the muzzle or magazine takes while held: about 5 kg

wall.rule: The body's bed-side wall, which everything stands on: ten layers

rail.rule: The barrel slot's floor and ceiling walls, either side of the disc's path
